messages.subject: simulation study using barrier model
parts:
Hello!
Experts.
I am conducting a simulation study, the simulated data is generated based on barrier model and the response variable follows Poisson distribution, finally the data is fitted with ordinary model and barrier model and spatial prediction is done, it is found that there is a big difference between the predicted value and the true value (u/population, which may be greater than 1，u is the mean value，population is the offset), especially for the larger true value, as shown in the figure. the RMSE is 9.84
I think the results are a bit strange, but can't find the reason.
Looking forward to your reply! Thanks!
The code is as follows

messages.author: 9a89594e7fcb7aad
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] simulation study using barrier model
parts:
##result
pred_index <- inla.stack.index(joint.stk, 'pred')$data
pred_stat = res.stat$summary.fitted.values[pred_index,"0.5quant"]
result <- data.frame(true_value = field.true, pred_value =
res.stat$summary.fitted.values[pred_index,"0.5quant"])
RMSE <- sqrt(mean((pred_stat-field.true)^2))


fitted.values are the mean of the poisson, ie exp(lin.predictor), while
field.true is on the lin.predictor scale. you need to bring them into
the same scale to compare. also note that the intercept is included, so
there is a constant missing if you want to compare.

Thank you for your reply.
As shown in the code below, field.true is indeed on the exp(lin.predictor) scale, and already include the  intercept. So I guess it's probably not that. 
##
  xlim = c(0, width)
  ylim = c(0, height)
  proj = inla.mesh.projector(mesh, xlim = xlim, ylim = ylim, dims = c(width*111/5, height*111/5))
  field.proj = inla.mesh.project(proj, exp(u*sqrt(sigma.u) + beta))
  field.true = field.proj[-which(proj$x>(width-gap)/2&proj$x<(width+gap)/2),]
  field.true = as.vector(field.true)
##
